claim: Migration a_delivery_event_follows_its_order exists exactly once and declares the AFTER UPDATE OF status, delivered_at trigger on procurement_orders, the AFTER INSERT trigger on calendar_events (an event born for an order that already arrived or will not come is closed at birth), and the order_id partial index the lookup uses; it holds no backfill (fork 1 of ADR 0284 is open)
verify: f=$(ls supabase/migrations/ | grep '_a_delivery_event_follows_its_order\.sql$'); [ "$(echo "$f" | grep -c .)" -eq 1 ] && f=supabase/migrations/$f && grep -q 'CREATE TRIGGER trg_procurement_order_moves_its_delivery_event' "$f" && grep -q 'AFTER UPDATE OF status, delivered_at ON public.procurement_orders' "$f" && grep -q 'CREATE TRIGGER trg_delivery_event_is_born_matching_its_order' "$f" && grep -q 'AFTER INSERT ON public.calendar_events' "$f" && grep -q 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_calendar_events_order_delivery' "$f" && ! grep -qE '^(UPDATE|INSERT|DELETE)[[:space:]]' "$f"

claim: procurement.service.ts carries no delivery-event closer of its own: closeDeliveryCalendarEvent, cancelCalendarEventForOrder and updateCalendarEventForDelivery are gone, and no .from("calendar_events") is followed by .update( (the table closes the event, ADR 0284)
verify: S=apps/api-gateway/src/procurement/procurement.service.ts; test -f $S && ! grep -qE 'closeDeliveryCalendarEvent|cancelCalendarEventForOrder|updateCalendarEventForDelivery' $S && python3 -c "import re,sys; s=open(sys.argv[1]).read(); sys.exit(1 if re.search(r'[.]from[(][[:space:]]*.calendar_events.[[:space:]]*[)][[:space:]]*[.]update[(]'.replace('[[:space:]]', chr(92)+'s'), s) else 0)" $S

claim: createCalendarEventForOrder places the delivery event on the order's own stated date: it takes statedDeliveryDate, reads it through statedDeliveryDayOf, uses it as event_date when it is a real day, and approveDraft hands it the row's expected_delivery_date (OrderResponseDto does not carry it); with no date it keeps approval + 7 and says so
verify: S=apps/api-gateway/src/procurement/procurement.service.ts; grep -q '^    statedDeliveryDate: string | null,$' $S && grep -q 'const stated = statedDeliveryDayOf(statedDeliveryDate);' $S && grep -q 'eventDate = stated;' $S && grep -q 'raw.expected_delivery_date ?? null,' $S && grep -q 'estimated 7 days after approval; the order states no date' $S

claim: procurement_agent.py no longer selects 'id, tags' from calendar_events (no such column) and has no _cancel_order_calendar_event; its out-of-stock message no longer tells the manager the delivery was removed from the calendar
verify: A=services/agent-orchestrator/agents/procurement_agent.py; test -f $A && ! grep -q '"id, tags"' $A && ! grep -q '_cancel_order_calendar_event' $A && ! grep -q 'removed from calendar' $A
